title: Why planes fly curves
hook: The straight line on a globe is a curve on a flat map.
notes: Distances are great-circle distances computed live. Real flight paths also follow winds, airspace and air-traffic rules. The southern Vienna–Tokyo route is schematic.

scenes.title: The shortest way
scenes.text: On a globe, the shortest path between two cities is a great circle. Here is Frankfurt to Los Angeles: straight over Greenland.

scenes.title: Now flatten it
scenes.text: Same line, flat map. It bends up towards the Arctic. Nothing changed but the projection.

scenes.title: The longest flight
scenes.text: New York to Singapore is one of the longest scheduled flights, around 15,000 km and close to 19 hours. Its shortest path runs close to the North Pole.

scenes.title: Vienna to Tokyo, then and now
scenes.text: Before 2022, flights crossed Siberia. Since Russia's airspace closed to European airlines, they detour south over Central Asia and China.
